_comment_2node: TWO-NODE variant of configs/grpo_coder30b_a3b_trloo_burst.json. Identical recipe -- same TRLOO advantage, same 16 trajectories, same rejection sampling, same lengths -- so a 2-node run stays comparable to the 1-node run it replaces. The ONLY change is fsdp_sharding_strategy. Launch with scripts/spur_grpo_2node.sbatch, which also forces configs/accelerate_fsdp_grpo_2node.yaml; that YAML is what actually makes the strategy take effect, because under FSDP1 accelerate wraps with `sharding_strategy or reshard_after_forward` and always exports FSDP_SHARDING_STRATEGY from its --config_file.
_comment_why_2_nodes_helps: num_trajectories is 16 and the rollout is partitioned by _rank_slice(G, rank, world), so world=8 gives every rank 2 trajectories to roll out serially while world=16 gives it 1. Both divide evenly, so neither is ragged (ragged per-rank counts deadlock generation). The rollout dominates a step -- measured ~90 minutes against a ~27 s inter-node gradient sync on the 4.5 GB/s Ethernet hop -- so halving the per-rank rollout is close to halving the step.
_comment_model_id: PRODUCTION RL TARGET, matching configs/sft_coder30b_a3b.json so the two stages train the same backbone. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct: 30.5B total / 3.3B active MoE (Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, 48 layers, 128 experts, 8 per token). The launcher REWRITES this to the SFT output via FROM_STAGE, exactly as configs/grpo_14b_full.json's Qwen/Qwen3-14B is rewritten to the DPO output; the value at rest names the backbone the lineage descends from so the config is readable on its own.
_comment_model_revision: The same hub commit configs/sft_coder30b_a3b.json pins, verified there against the downloaded snapshot (16 shards, 18,867 tensors, all BF16, 30,532,122,624 parameters). Carried here so that a run launched WITHOUT a FROM_STAGE rewrite -- a bring-up smoke against the raw backbone -- is still pinned rather than taking whatever the shared HF cache happens to hold.
_comment_advantage_estimator: The reason this config exists. GRPO centres every sample on a group mean that contains that sample, and build_kevin_samples pools m trajectories x n turns into one group, so the baseline for turn t of trajectory i also contains the LATER turns of trajectory i -- which are downstream of the action being credited. Measured by exact enumeration in tests/test_trloo_advantages.py: pooled centring returns exactly (M-1)/M of the true gradient, the std term's error GROWS with the group instead of shrinking, and on asymmetric multi-turn MDPs the expected gradient can point the WRONG WAY (worst case found: true +0.171, GRPO -0.007, GRPO+std -0.098, TRLOO +0.171). TRLOO centres each sample on the mean of the OTHER trajectories at the SAME turn, which is independent of the credited action and therefore unbiased.
_comment_variance_floor: 0.0, and it MUST be 0.0 here. TRLOO never calls avspo_advantages, so the AVSPO variance floor and its virtual samples would be an inert request -- kore.policy.capabilities.audit_requested_capabilities reports exactly that, and scripts/spur_grpo_1node.sbatch runs the audit with KORE_GRPO_INERT_FEATURES=error. It is also the right value on the merits: the floor injects virtual samples into the NORMALISATION statistics, and every self-inclusive statistic is what biases the estimator in the first place. TRLOO is deliberately unnormalised; gradient scale is handled by max_grad_norm.
_comment_num_trajectories: Dr. Kernel's reported defaults: ROLLOUT_N=16 trajectories per group, MAX_TURN=3 turns per trajectory. num_turns mirrors max_tool_turns because agentic=true routes every rollout through AgentHarness, whose horizon is max_tool_turns; leaving them different would state a horizon the run does not use. tasks_per_step is 4 rather than the 14B recipe's 8: each step rolls 16 trajectories x 3 turns per task and every turn compiles and benches on the same node, and this backbone's per-rank memory is far larger, so the step cost is dominated by rollout rather than by the update.
_comment_learning_rate: 1e-6, Dr. Kernel's reported default, and half the 14B recipe's 2e-6. Lower is the right direction for two independent reasons: this is a 30.5B MoE where only 3.3B parameters are active per token, so each expert sees a fraction of the batch and a given LR moves it further per update than it would a dense model; and RL follows an SFT stage that has not been evaluated yet, so the first RL run should be the conservative one.
_comment_dual_clip_c: 3.0. The clipped surrogate is bounded above for a positive advantage but NOT below for a negative one: as the ratio grows, r*A falls without limit and one sample can own the whole gradient (tests/test_grpo_stability.py measures -1e6 at ratio 1e6). The floor caps the worst single-sample loss at c*|A|. With ppo_epochs=1 the ratio is ~1 by construction so this should never bind; it costs nothing when it does not, and this run cannot be babysat across the many allocations a 2000-step RL job spans.
_comment_mismatch_correction: false. The correction is real -- the sharded loop generates on a plain full-weight per-rank replica and trains through the FSDP wrapper, so the same weights are evaluated on different code paths -- but with ppo_epochs=1 the measured weight sits within about a percent of 1.0, and enabling a correction the run does not need would state a capability that changes nothing. The DIAGNOSTIC is what matters here and is unconditional: _grpo_step_mismatch_stat reports the mean and max weight, and a mean that drifts or a max pinned at the cap is a bug report about rollout/training divergence.
_comment_clip_ratio_low: Inherited from the 14B recipe and for the same reason: KORE's importance ratio is length-normalised (token-MEAN logprob, i.e. the GSPO sequence ratio), so DAPO's 0.2/0.28 token-level bounds never bind -- a legitimate sequence ratio sits within ~1% of 1.0. These are sequence-scale bounds, and with ppo_epochs=1 they are defense-in-depth rather than an active lever.
_comment_rejection_sampling: MRS is live: _apply_mrs runs in both the single-process and the sharded group assembly, and expresses a rejection through the same traj_infra mechanism build_kevin_samples already uses to drop a turn, so a rejected trajectory contributes no policy-gradient term and no advantage without a second parallel drop path. geometric aggregation is Dr. Kernel's reported default and is the right aggregator on the merits: the geometric mean is dominated by the WEAKEST turn and collapses to zero if any turn is zero, so one strong turn cannot carry a trajectory that was broken for the rest of the episode (on [0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 0.0] the arithmetic mean still reads 0.675). mrs_min_quality stays 0.0 so the only rejections are the structural ones -- never correct, or a gamed measurement -- rather than a hand-picked cutoff on a reward scale this lineage has not measured. PRS's coverage rejections need a kernel trace, which is not armed here (see profiling_reward_weight), so prs_require_profile MUST be false: requiring a profile that is never collected would reject every candidate, and the audit reports exactly that combination.
_comment_prs_min_coverage: 0.0, which leaves the zero-coverage decoy rejection on and the lazy-optimisation rejection off. PRS is not invoked anywhere in kore/ today -- only MRS is -- so this value is inert, and it is set correctly NOW so that wiring PRS up does not silently inherit a threshold that rejects correct work. Measured on gfx950 (docs/evidence/coverage_denominator.md): coverage is computed on the candidate over a denominator that still contains fixed harness cost, so it tracks the kernel's SLOWNESS rather than its share of any workload. Ten correct seed kernels spanned 0.036 to 0.587, so 0.1 rejected correct gen_relu_fp32 and softmax_bf16 as lazy, while a deliberately 46x-slowed kernel measured 0.739 and passed. Raise this only once coverage is measured over a delimited benched region.
_comment_profiling_reward_weight: 0.0, and this is the one deliberately UNARMED lever in this recipe. The machinery is complete: KoreEnv.collect_kernel_trace runs the candidate under rocprofv3 --kernel-trace, kore.reward.coverage turns the dispatches into a coverage share and combines it with the measured speedup by Amdahl's law, and _coverage_bonus adds a bounded term plus turn feedback. The collector is now CONFIRMED to work on this hardware -- gfx950, rocprofiler-sdk 1.1.0, 22-column kernel_trace.csv exactly as documented, decoy detection exact -- and scripts/make_ktrace_receipt.py produces the receipt. It stays at 0.0 anyway, and the reason changed rather than went away: the trace is trustworthy but the coverage MAGNITUDE built on it is not Amdahl's p. Coverage is measured on the candidate over a denominator that still includes fixed harness cost, so it rises as the kernel gets SLOWER -- a correct seed read 0.057 and a 46x slower copy of it read 0.739, which through amdahl_end_to_end_speedup pays the slow one more (docs/evidence/coverage_denominator.md). Amdahl's p is a property of the baseline workload and must not depend on the candidate. Arming this needs the timed region delimited (roctx ranges, or an --iters 0 setup trace to subtract) plus a HIP kernel-name source, since all six hip_* tasks sampled produced no trace at all. The intended value once that lands is 0.15, strictly below correctness_weight so shaping can never outrank correctness.
_comment_max_plausible_speedup: The cap above which a claimed speedup is treated as a gamed measurement rather than a kernel, applied at REWARD time and not only at data-selection time. 12.0 is the value kore.data.agentic_filter.FilterPolicy already derives from the observed distribution (2x the measured p99, floored) rather than a third hand-picked number, so the RL-time guard and the data-time guard agree. The 1541.94x that reached an early SFT mixture from third-party data is the failure this exists for; real fused wins against a production AITER/hipBLASLt baseline land in the low single digits.
_comment_kevin_best_kernel_scoring: Unchanged from the 14B recipe: trajectory value is the best CORRECT kernel, gamma propagates later success back to the turns that set it up, and credit_incorrect_turns keeps the shaped sub-threshold signal on incorrect turns instead of a hard zero so the gradient is not flat across the not-yet-correct band. Note this is deliberately NOT the same signal MRS uses to judge trajectories: rejection zeroes an incorrect turn hard, which is what makes the geometric aggregate collapse, while the training reward keeps its shaped credit. Conflating the two would undo the densification.
_comment_max_prompt_length: 4096 / 1024, reduced from 17408 / 17408 because the original values are MEASURED to fail. See _comment_fsdp_sharding_strategy for the four data points. This pair is the only configuration that completed a real 30B rollout+update step on one 8x gfx950 node: peak 199.2 GB allocated per rank, 217003 of 258048 MiB device (84%), reward_mean 0.6648, grad_norm 0.5138, mismatch_mean 1.001. The cost is real and should not be understated: an agentic transcript is task prompt plus prior turns plus verifier feedback, so 4096 will truncate multi-turn trajectories that 17408 would have held, and truncation shows up as overlong masking rather than as an error. Raising it needs chunked log-probs (the transient is logits of seq x 151936 vocab, 18.3 GiB at 21504 tokens once cross-entropy upcasts to fp32), a second node, or measured offload -- plus a resolution of the checkpoint recompute error at 8192.
_comment_starpo_s: Kept on. StarPO-S drops collapsed groups and DAPO dynamic sampling REFILLS to keep the effective batch stable instead of shrinking the update. These are the group-level complement to MRS: StarPO-S judges whether a group carries contrast at all, MRS judges trajectories within a group and DECLINES when filtering would remove that contrast.
_comment_rc_grpo: Each of these is off because THIS topology cannot deliver it, and kore.policy.capabilities.validate_grpo_config rejects the combination outright rather than letting it look active. rc_grpo: reward-control tokens reach only the serial _rollout, and this recipe is agentic. sc_grpo: the SC-GRPO block exists only in the single-process loop, and this recipe is distributed. value_prefilter: only the serial _rollout calls _prefilter_bench_indices, and there is no trained value artifact for this lineage anyway -- so num_candidates_per_turn and value_prefilter_k are pinned to 1, which is the real per-turn bench economy rather than the 8/4 dataclass defaults.
_comment_physics_shaping_weight: 0.0, on the same evidence as the 14B recipe. _physics_shaping_weight() returns 0.0 unless BOTH physics_shaping_evidence_path and physics_shaping_evidence_fingerprint are set, and docs/P0_RESULTS.md records three independent studies all deciding INTEGRITY_ONLY with 'authorized families: none'. No evidence document that passes the gate can be written from the data that exists, and writing one anyway would fabricate the artifact the gate exists to demand. physics_live_counters is therefore false too: counter collection is nested INSIDE the shaping gate, so requesting it here would ask for per-turn rocprofv3 profiling that never runs.
_comment_use_search: use_search, coevolve and their children are OFF for this config, unlike configs/grpo_14b_full.json which turns them on. Not a downgrade -- a scoping decision. Every one of them mines an archive built by the 14B lineage (data/b05factory), and this is a different backbone whose SFT stage has not run, so there is no measured baseline for this policy against which a curriculum or a distillation sink means anything. Turning them on would make the first RL run on a new model simultaneously the first run of five unvalidated levers, and any result would be unattributable. They are re-enabled once this recipe has a clean TRLOO baseline to compare against, which is also when coevolve_distill_path gets a root that belongs to this lineage.
_comment_ref_checkpoint: The post-SFT checkpoint, per the field's contract in kore/policy/configs.py, and NOT the checkpoint GRPO trains from. For this lineage those are the same directory -- there is no DPO stage between SFT and RL on this backbone -- so ref_checkpoint intentionally equals the launcher's FROM_STAGE default. That is a real difference from the 14B recipe, where anchoring to the DPO output would have measured drift from a preference-tuned model instead of from the broad post-SFT policy. Here the post-SFT policy IS the run's starting point, so the k3 anchor measures drift from the run's own start, which is what retention means when RL follows SFT directly. It has not been trained yet, so the audit will report it as an ARTIFACT finding until runs/sft_coder30b_a3b exists.
_comment_save_total_limit: save_total_limit is 2, raised from 1 on the same corrected arithmetic as the SFT config. Adam keeps ~16 bytes/param, so a 30.5B checkpoint is ~488GB against the 14B's ~221GB, and because the Trainer writes the new checkpoint BEFORE rotating the old one out, limit=2 peaks near ~1.46TB. The premise that forced 1 was that the volume had ~1090GB free and could not hold two; /shared_nfs actually has 42T, so the peak is 3.5% of it. limit=1 was the riskier setting for exactly the reason this run needs it not to be: the rotation window is a period with no complete checkpoint on disk, and total_steps 1000 is a horizon no 23h allocation finishes, so this run WILL be preempted and eventually inside that window. save_steps 50 rather than the 14B's 100 because a step here is far more expensive, so 50 steps is already hours of work to lose. The launcher's requeue plus _discover_grpo_resume carry the run across allocations -- which only works if there is something resumable to find.
_comment_save_archive_every: 25, lowered from 250 once a step was measured rather than assumed. At ~62-90 min/step, 250 puts the first pinned checkpoint ~11 days out while save_total_limit 2 rotates everything older away, so the run would spend its first fortnight with nothing archived. That matters most here because ref_anchor_coef is 0.0 -- nothing tethers the policy to the post-SFT model -- and RL trains on kernel tasks ONLY, the single-domain setup OLMo 3 reports over-optimises. Every drift instrument (checkpoint_ab, retention, heldout_lm) scores a CHECKPOINT against a reference, and stage-4 WiSE-FT (kore.policy.soup) interpolates FROM checkpoints, so archives are what make the retention-gated alpha sweep a real search instead of a single end-of-run point.
_comment_fsdp: fsdp_transformer_layer_cls is set explicitly, exactly as configs/sft_coder30b_a3b.json does. Two things make this load-bearing. TRANSFORMER_BASED_WRAP with a class name matching nothing wraps NOTHING, so FSDP degrades to one flat parameter for the whole model and either OOMs or loses every overlap -- and it does so silently. And configs/accelerate_fsdp_grpo.yaml still hardcodes the DENSE Qwen3DecoderLayer: build_fsdp_plugin's explicitly-constructed plugin does override that env value (verified), and detect_transformer_layer_cls already maps an A3B id to Qwen3MoeDecoderLayer, but relying on two fallbacks to correct a wrong literal is not a contract. cpu_offload stays false: SHARD_GRAD_OP keeps params resident per rank, which is exactly what lets the co-located rollout generate locally, and offloading them would defeat that.
_comment_cpu_offload: Memory, resolved but still unmeasured. The sharded GRPO loop holds a full-weight rollout REPLICA per rank, ~61GB at 30.5B bf16, plus sharded training params, gradients and optimizer state. It previously ALSO held a frozen KL-anchor replica for another ~61GB -- ~122GB per rank before any training state -- which ref_anchor_coef=0.0 now removes. That halves the static footprint and is the single change that makes this recipe plausible on one node. It is still not a claim that it fits: no measured peak profile exists, KORE_RESOURCE_PREFLIGHT=report in scripts/spur_grpo_1node.sbatch reports rather than gates, and anyone launching this must read the first step's gpu_mem_snapshot before assuming the remaining 999 will run. If it still does not fit, cpu_offload=true is the next lever, at the cost of the local rollout.
_comment_strict_feature_validation: false, for the same structural reason as the 14B recipe: capabilities._UNSUPPORTED_STRICT_FEATURES refuses several research levers outright, so strict mode is a different lane rather than a stronger version of this one. What replaces it is not nothing -- audit_requested_capabilities runs unconditionally at train_grpo startup, the launcher promotes its findings to a hard failure via KORE_GRPO_INERT_FEATURES=error, and tests/test_grpo_30b_moe_config.py fails CI if this config ever requests a capability that is provably inert from its own text.
_comment_ref_anchor_coef: 0.0, not 0.001. Any value above zero makes grpo.py load a frozen reference replica for the KL anchor -- 61GB per rank at 30.5B bf16, on top of the rollout replica, so ~122GB per rank before a single byte of training state. At 0.001 that memory bought a term contributing ~0.1% of the loss gradient: the full price of a reference policy for essentially no regularisation. Dropping KL entirely is standard in reasoning RL rather than a shortcut -- DAPO removes it explicitly to avoid the reference network, and the argument is that KL exists to keep an RLHF policy near its initial model, which is the opposite of what we want from a model that must acquire a capability it does not have. Stability comes from TRLOO's dual-clip ratio clipping and truncated importance sampling instead, which are the modern replacements. Set this above zero only with the memory measured first.
_comment_fsdp_sharding_strategy: MEASURED 2026-08-16 on 8x gfx950 (252 GiB HBM each) with the real Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct weights at the pinned revision, one full rollout+update step through scripts/launch_distributed.sh. This replaces the accounting-only claim that this recipe MIGHT fit. Three data points, all with num_trajectories=8 (one trajectory per rank; the recipe's 16 is two per rank and strictly worse): (a) max_prompt 17408 / max_response 4096 under fsdp_sharding_strategy shard_grad_op (ZeRO-2, the previous behaviour) -- OOM on all 8 ranks, HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES with 'Available Free mem : 0 MB', device peak 257904 of 258048 MiB; (b) the SAME config under full_shard (ZeRO-3), which takes the policy's replicated 61 GiB down to ~7.6 GiB per rank -- ALSO OOM, device peak 257594 MiB, which refutes parameters as the binding term; (c) max_prompt 4096 / max_response 1024 under full_shard -- COMPLETED, peak allocated 199.2 GB per rank, device peak 217003 MiB (84% of HBM, ~40 GiB headroom), reward_mean 0.6648, grad_norm 0.5138, mismatch_mean 1.001. So the wall is SEQUENCE LENGTH, not parameter footprint: freeing 53 GiB of params changed nothing while cutting the sequence fixed it. The transient is the log-prob recompute, which materialises logits of seq x 151936 vocab (18.3 GiB at 21504 tokens once cross-entropy upcasts to fp32) on top of activations, per sample, with no chunking. Raising max_prompt_length back toward 17408 requires either chunked log-probs, a second node, or measured offload -- not an argument. A fourth point, added after the three above: max_prompt 8192 / max_response 2048 under full_shard did NOT OOM (device peak 221178 MiB) but died with torch.utils.checkpoint.CheckpointError -- recomputed activations had different metadata than the forward. That is a SECOND, distinct failure mode above the proven point, and on a 128-expert MoE the obvious suspect is routing differing between the forward and the recompute. It is unresolved and must be understood before max_prompt_length is raised; a longer context is not merely a memory question here.
_comment_save_steps_burst: save_steps=5 because burst's per-job ceiling is 12h (measured: 12:00:00 runs, 1-00:00:00 refused with QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit). At ~1.5h/step a 12h allocation is ~8 steps, so a checkpoint every 5 steps (~7.5h) guarantees one durable save per allocation with margin before the 11h self-requeue.
_comment_fsdp_sharding_strategy_2node: hybrid_shard = FULL_SHARD within a node, REPLICATE across nodes. These nodes have no RDMA fabric (one Ethernet interface, and every GRPO log carries 'Could not find any local path from gpu N to net'); a 16-rank inter-node all_reduce measured 4.5 GB/s against hundreds of GB/s for intra-node xGMI. FULL_SHARD across nodes would re-gather parameters over that link on every forward and backward, making two nodes SLOWER than one. Hybrid leaves exactly one gradient all-reduce per step on the slow hop, and its shard group is the same 8 GPUs that measured 199.2 GiB/rank here.
_comment_save_steps: 2, lowered from 5 after a MEASURED loss. Job 24465 ran four healthy steps and died at step 4 on a collective timeout -- one step short of its first checkpoint -- so every step it completed was thrown away and the resubmit restarted at 0. save_steps is insurance against exactly that, and 5 was priced for a step that was assumed cheaper and a job that was assumed not to die. At the measured ~62 min/step on two nodes (~90 on one) a checkpoint every 2 steps banks progress roughly every 2-3 hours, so a crash costs at most one step instead of the whole allocation. The cost is real and accepted: a consolidated 30B checkpoint is ~488GB, and with save_total_limit 2 the rotation peak is ~1.46TB against 94TB free on /shared_nfs, plus a few minutes of NFS write per save. Losing 100% of a 12h allocation is the more expensive failure.
